QP-2890-verification
# Xsolla AI Toolkit

Agent skills for Xsolla — works with Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex CLI, Windsurf, Roo Code, Augment, and more.

Install the kit in your AI coding tool and your agent can integrate Xsolla's APIs directly into your game, or build a fully functional headless web shop you own and host with full control of the frontend. It works with the AI coding tools you already use, with no engine lock-in and no proprietary assistant. Instead of generating code that looks right but breaks in production, your agent follows validated, production-ready logic encoding the correct integration paths, so the first AI-assisted attempt is the right one, with validation built in. From setting up a project and configuring a catalog to integrating Pay Station and implementing webhooks, the kit takes you from zero to a working integration.

## What's inside

| Directory | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `skills/` | SKILL.md files — one per Xsolla domain |
| `AGENTS.md` | Universal context loaded automatically by most agents |
| `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | GitHub Copilot-specific context |
| `.cursor/skills/` | Cursor-native skills (synced from `skills/`) |
| `.cursor/rules/` | Short always-on Cursor pointer rule |
| `docs/` | Architecture, distribution, and skill-gap guides |

## Quick start

Install the kit as a plugin in your preferred coding agent, or copy it into your project for any tool that follows the [AGENTS.md](https://agents.md) convention:

### Claude Code

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit && claude plugin install xsolla-ai-kit@xsolla-ai-kit
```

Or in a session:

```text
/plugin marketplace add xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit
/plugin install xsolla-ai-kit@xsolla-ai-kit
```

### Cursor

Add this repo as a workspace folder (or open it as the project), then use natural language — Cursor loads skills from `.cursor/skills/`.

```text
# Example
Integrate Xsolla Headless Checkout and let me pay with a credit card in sandbox
```

For an end-to-end shop, start with `shop-setup`. A short always-on rule in `.cursor/rules/xsolla-ai-kit.mdc` points the agent at those skills.

### Codex

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit
```

### Gemini CLI

```bash
gemini extensions install https://github.com/xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit
```

### Other tools (Windsurf, Roo Code, Augment, Amp, Copilot, …)

For tools with no official plugin system, use the kit by copying `AGENTS.md` and the `skills/` directory into your project root. Any tool that follows the [AGENTS.md](https://agents.md) convention will pick the skills up automatically the next time you open the project:

---
name: quest-setup
description: >-
  Creates, inspects and edits Xsolla Quest Platform quests conversationally,
  submits a quest event, and verifies that the event actually made the quest
  execute. Covers the whole quest document: the node graph and its connections,
  the seven node subtypes, the condition grammar, activation limits, and all
  nine reward types including web3_item and web3_token ERC-20 payouts. Use when
  setting up a quest, adding a trigger or a condition, attaching a reward,
  editing or activating an existing quest, firing a test event, or working out
  why a quest did not fire — including "create a quest", "add a Web3 reward to
  my quest", "make a quest that pays USDC", "trigger my quest", "send a quest
  event", "why didn't my quest complete", "list my quests", "activate a quest",
  "quest platform API".
metadata:
  owner: r.aliyev
  domain: quests
  status: draft
---

## Status

This skill is a **draft**. The credential lane it targets is not deployed yet;
see Prerequisites.

## When to use

Use this skill when the developer wants to manage quests on the Xsolla Quest
Platform:

- Create a quest, as a draft first and then activate it
- Add triggers, conditions or reward actions to a quest
- List, view or edit existing quests
- Submit a single quest event to make a quest run
- Check whether an event actually caused a quest to execute

Out of scope: on-chain finality, wallet balances and Backpack display. This
skill configures a Web3 reward and reports that a quest executed. For a Web3
reward, a completed reward action means the provider returned a transaction
hash for the claim. The skill never states that a token was delivered.

## Prerequisites

Follow [`references/auth-and-environment.md`](references/auth-and-environment.md)
for the required credential, request authentication, internal hosts, and scope
confirmation.

**This credential lane is not accepted yet.** Quest Platform implements it in
QP-2862, inside QP-2858 Phase 3, which depends on Phases 1 and 2. Until it
lands, authenticated qp-server CRUD requests using this Basic lane return 401.
OpenAPI discovery remains available without credentials on stage, so do not
mistake schema discovery for CRUD readiness. If another credential lane is
provided, verify it against the live contract rather than assuming it works.
Say exactly which lane failed, naming the ticket when it is QP-2862, rather than
reporting a generic authentication failure. For qp-data execution read-back, follow
[`references/auth-and-environment.md`](references/auth-and-environment.md)
for current access requirements.

## Source of truth

Follow this order. It is the rule the rest of the skill depends on.

1. **Routes, path parameters, envelope field names and types, and the
   top-level `required` list** come from the service's **live OpenAPI
   document**. Fetch it once at the start of the session.
2. **Node subtypes, node `parameters`, the condition grammar, the reward
   bodies, conditionally required fields, and every enum the document renders
   as a bare `string`** come from this skill's `references/`.
3. On conflict: the OpenAPI document wins on shape, `references/` wins on
   rules. Rules that only the server's hand-written validator enforces are
   marked as such where they appear.
4. If neither source answers the question, **ask the developer**. Do not infer
   a field by analogy with another Xsolla API.

If a host is unreachable, which usually means no corporate network, say so and
offer to continue on `references/` alone, noting that the envelope may have
drifted. Never continue silently.

## Reference material

content.content:
- [`references/auth-and-environment.md`](references/auth-and-environment.md) — hosts, credential, scope, and the incoming auth changes
- [`references/quest-document.md`](references/quest-document.md) — the quest graph, conditional requirements, full-document PUT
- [`references/node-subtypes.md`](references/node-subtypes.md) — the seven accepted node subtypes and their parameters
- [`references/conditions.md`](references/conditions.md) — condition grammar: types, operands, operators, event counting
- [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md) — the nine reward types and their bodies, including web3_token
- [`references/events.md`](references/events.md) — submitting a quest event to qp-events-collector
- [`references/verification.md`](references/verification.md) — reading execution results back from qp-data

## Flow

1. **Bring-up.** Fetch the OpenAPI documents. Check the credential is set. List
   quests, show the resolved scope, and get confirmation.
2. **Draft.** Create the quest as `inactive` with the four required fields.
3. **Fill in.** Add nodes and edges one at a time, asking for each missing
   required value. Show the assembled document before sending it.
4. **Activate.** A separate step: move to `active` with dates, after checking
   there are at least two nodes, a trigger-to-action path, no intended orphan
   nodes, and an acyclic graph. For a Web3 reward, also run the read-only
   checks in [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md): SKU, amount
   units, and the recipient's wallet. Show the activation limits and the
   effective repeat behavior before asking for confirmation.
5. **Edit.** Read, change, full `PUT`. Warn that `PUT` replaces the whole
   document.
6. **Event.** Build the payload, generate a fresh UUID `idempotency_key`, set
   an RFC3339 `client_timestamp`, confirm with the developer, and submit to
   qp-events-collector.
7. **Verify.** Read the execution back from qp-data, correlate its `eventId`
   with the collector's returned `event_id` as described in
   [`references/verification.md`](references/verification.md), and report
   whether that event made the quest run and which action nodes completed.
   If an action `FAILED`, report its `error` verbatim. Do not report a reward
   as delivered.

## Safety stops

- Read back and show the resolved scope before the first write, and get
  confirmation.
- Before activation, show every externally observable action and get explicit
  confirmation for its impact. An `issue_reward` can create real payouts;
  `send_http_webhook` sends event data to an external URL;
  `send_xsolla_app_notification` sends a user notification. Do not activate a
  `webshop_personalization` node as if it were a working personalization action.
- If `activation_limits` is absent, ask the developer to explicitly choose
  unlimited repeat behavior and acknowledge that every qualifying event may run
  the action. Do not silently choose a limit or omit this decision.
- Ask for confirmation before submitting an event.
- After an uncertain event response, such as a timeout, **do not resend** —
  neither with the same idempotency key nor with a new one. A timeout is not a
  failure. Report "result unknown" and stop.
- After a `FAILED` reward action, do not resend the event. Fix the quest, then
  send a new event with a new key only after the developer confirms.
- If a Web3 reward action is stuck in `RUNNING` or failed on a timeout, do not
  send another event. The claim has no idempotency key and may already have
  paid; see [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md).
- Never claim a reward was delivered.

## Errors

Branch on the HTTP status only. The API has no stable machine-readable error
codes.

| Status | What to tell the developer |
|---|---|
| 401 | Missing or invalid credential. For the credential lane described in the reference, name QP-2862. |
| 403 | The key lacks the required `questconfig:*` capability. |
| 404 | "Not found, or no access, or the project is not onboarded to Quest Platform." Never say the quest does not exist. |
| 409 | Conflict. |
| 422 | Validation failed. Show `detail` verbatim. |

1. **Bring-up.** Fetch the OpenAPI documents. Check the credential is set. List

3. **Fill in.** Add nodes and edges one at a time, asking for each missing
   required value. Show the assembled document before sending it.
4. **Activate.** A separate step: move to `active` with dates, after checking
   there are at least two nodes, a trigger-to-action path, no intended orphan
   nodes, and an acyclic graph. For a Web3 reward, also run the read-only
   checks in [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md): SKU, amount
   units, and the recipient's wallet. Show the activation limits and the
   effective repeat behavior before asking for confirmation.
5. **Edit.** Read, change, full `PUT`. Warn that `PUT` replaces the whole
   document.
6. **Event.** Build the payload, generate a fresh UUID `idempotency_key`, set
   an RFC3339 `client_timestamp`, confirm with the developer, and submit to
   qp-events-collector.

   with the collector's returned `event_id` as described in

   whether that event made the quest run and which action nodes completed.

   as delivered.

  confirmation.

  confirmation for its impact. An `issue_reward` can create real payouts;

  the action. Do not silently choose a limit or omit this decision.

  neither with the same idempotency key nor with a new one. A timeout is not a

options.label: Agent tool subagent
options.description: Сабагент через Agent tool, ему дают путь к SKILL.md и он его читает. Быстрее, но это не реальная установка плагина и частично наследует окружение.

options.label: Copy AGENTS.md + skills/

options.label: Full live via X-REQUEST-APIKEY

options.label: Offline / mocked
options.description: Без сети: мок-сервер по OpenAPI или только проверка, что агент строит правильные запросы и соблюдает safety stops.

# quest-setup skill: e2e validation via subagents

## Context
`xsolla-ai-kit/skills/quest-setup` (local branch `QP-2890-verification`, not pushed; it has diverged from PR stack #38→#46) has not been tested against a live stage yet. Goal: build a list of use cases and run each one e2e with a fresh subagent that works from the skill alone. The coordinator plays the developer over SendMessage. The whole path runs through to a web3 reward being paid out. Every issue gets logged, fixed by a separate subagent, and retested until clean.

Rule: all research, investigation and hands-on work runs in subagents. The main context holds only short summaries, and the details live in files in the scratchpad (`$SCRATCH/e2e/`).

## Known facts (read-only probes, 2026-09-24)
- The OpenAPI for qp-server, qp-events-collector and qp-data is available. qp-server now has `/api/v2/projects/{project_id}/quests`, and Basic is recognised ("only accepted on project-scoped routes"). So `references/auth-and-environment.md` is **out of date**. That is the expected first finding.
- Lane A (primary for e2e): `X-REQUEST-APIKEY` service key for account "Rauf sandbox" (`f1a5f475…`, workspace `a2ac5c42…`, `xsolla_project_id: null`).
- Lane B: Basic `939308:<project key>` on project 316111 returns 404 "Project not found" (the same as with a wrong key). Cause is unknown.
- Keys came from the user in chat. They are passed to subagents only in the prompt/env and are never written into the repo or the plan.

## Phase 0: environment recon (1 Explore/general subagent, read-only)
Output: `$SCRATCH/e2e/env-facts.md`:
- the account scope under Lane A (list quests, account_id/publisher_id/project_id);
- the events-collector and qp-data auth requirements (check the actual responses);
- minting reads: `/currency-bindings`, `/skus`, and a test `xsolla_id` with a wallet (`GET /wallet/{id}`);
- why Lane B returns 404 (qp-server code in `adtech`: the Basic verifier and the project onboarding criterion);
- the diff between the live OpenAPI and `references/*`.
Nothing is written to stage. If Lane A doesn't work either, I stop and come to you.

## Phase 1: use case catalog (1 subagent → `$SCRATCH/e2e/use-cases.md`)
Built from SKILL.md, the references and env-facts. Each UC has: the developer's prompt, the scripted developer answers, expected skill behavior, and pass criteria. Draft:

**1. Project API key (Basic), проект 316111**
```
GET https://qp-server.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local/api/v2/projects/316111/quests?limit=2
Authorization: Basic base64("939308:ac6f5b53…")
→ 404 {"error":"Project not found"}
```
То же самое с username `316111` вместо `939308` и с `?publisherID=939308`. С заведомо неверным ключом ответ тоже 404. Значит, по этому ответу нельзя понять, отклонён ключ или проект 316111 не подключён к Quest Platform (так задумано в Phase 3). На маршруте без scope `/api/v2/quests` Basic отдаёт 401 "only accepted on project-scoped routes", так что этот lane на stage реально задеплоен.

**2. Service key (X-REQUEST-APIKEY), аккаунт "Rauf sandbox"**
```
GET https://qp-server.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local/api/v2/quests?limit=1
X-REQUEST-APIKEY: [REDACTED:credential]…
→ 401 {"error":"Invalid API key"}
```
Похоже, stage не видит этот ключ. Возможно, запись есть только в другой базе (dev или local), или сервер ждёт ключ в другом виде.

Сейчас ни одни креды не проходят. В main context я дальше не копаю. Первым шагом плана (Phase 0) пойдёт отдельный read-only сабагент. Он проверит в коде qp-server (`adtech`), как на stage проверяются Basic и `X-REQUEST-APIKEY` и что значит «проект подключён». Потом сверит это с ответами stage и вернёт короткий вывод. entries.name: ExitPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

Do not edit files, do not commit, do not switch branches in the user's checkout (use `git show`/`git log`/`git grep <ref>` or a throwaway `git worktree add` under /private/tmp/claude-501/ if you must). Do not send any write requests (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) to any stage service.

Code-search rule (mandatory): your first code-search move must be an actual call to a `neuronet_code_search` tool (Neuronet MCP, action=search) if it exists in your tools. If it fails or isn't available, silently fall back to normal Grep/Glob/git grep.

## Problem
The user was told the Quest Platform stage accepts their credentials, but both lanes fail on qp-server stage (`https://qp-server.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local`, internal network, use `curl -sk`):

1. Basic lane (publisher project API key):

# quest-setup skill: e2e validation via subagents

## Context
`xsolla-ai-kit/skills/quest-setup` (local branch `QP-2890-verification`, not pushed; it has diverged from PR stack #38→#46) has not been tested against a live stage yet. Goal: build a list of use cases and run each one e2e with a fresh subagent that works from the skill alone. The coordinator plays the developer over SendMessage. The whole path runs through to a web3 reward being paid out. Every issue gets logged, fixed by a separate subagent, and retested until clean.

Rule: all research, investigation and hands-on work runs in subagents. The main context holds only short summaries, and the details live in files in the scratchpad (`$SCRATCH/e2e/`).

## Known facts (read-only probes, 2026-09-24)
- The OpenAPI for qp-server, qp-events-collector and qp-data is available. qp-server now has `/api/v2/projects/{project_id}/quests`, and Basic is recognised ("only accepted on project-scoped routes"). So `references/auth-and-environment.md` is **out of date**. That is the expected first finding.
- Lane A (primary for e2e): `X-REQUEST-APIKEY` service key for account "Rauf sandbox" (`f1a5f475…`, workspace `a2ac5c42…`, `xsolla_project_id: null`).
- Lane B: Basic `939308:<project key>` on project 316111 returns 404 "Project not found" (the same as with a wrong key). Cause is unknown.
- Keys came from the user in chat. They are passed to subagents only in the prompt/env and are never written into the repo or the plan.

## Phase 0: environment recon (1 Explore/general subagent, read-only)
Output: `$SCRATCH/e2e/env-facts.md`:
- the account scope under Lane A (list quests, account_id/publisher_id/project_id);
- the events-collector and qp-data auth requirements (check the actual responses);
- minting reads: `/currency-bindings`, `/skus`, and a test `xsolla_id` with a wallet (`GET /wallet/{id}`);
- why Lane B returns 404 (qp-server code in `adtech`: the Basic verifier and the project onboarding criterion);
- the diff between the live OpenAPI and `references/*`.
Nothing is written to stage. If Lane A doesn't work either, I stop and come to you.

## Phase 1: use case catalog (1 subagent → `$SCRATCH/e2e/use-cases.md`)
Built from SKILL.md, the references and env-facts. Each UC has: the developer's prompt, the scripted developer answers, expected skill behavior, and pass criteria. Draft:
0. Install smoke: `claude plugin marketplace add <local repo>` + install + `claude plugin validate`, and the skill is discoverable
1. Bring-up: OpenAPI, credential check, list, scope confirmation
2. Create an `inactive` draft quest
3. Trigger + condition + non-web3 reward, then activation with activation_limits
4. Activation without activation_limits: the skill has to ask
5. Edit via full PUT (with the warning)
6. **web3_token (ERC-20)**: create → activate → event → verify → tx hash, without claiming "delivered"
7. **web3_item (NFT)**: the same
8. Event + verify for an existing quest (eventId correlation)
9. "Why didn't my quest complete": the condition didn't match
10. Errors: 404 (uniform wording), 422 (detail verbatim), Lane B
11. Safety: external actions (webhook/notification) require confirmation; timeout means no resend
12. Cleanup: deactivating test quests
I'll show the catalog to you in a short form before running it.

## Phase 2: runs (a fresh subagent per UC)
- Each run starts with a clean `general-purpose` subagent with no context from this session. It deploys the kit from the local branch into a clean temp project the way the README describes, loads the skill, and acts as the developer's agent.
- Every question from the skill goes back to me as its final message. I answer via SendMessage following the UC script, and I improvise when the skill asks for something not in the script (that is a finding too).
- Stateful UCs (2→3→5, 6, 7, 8, 9) run **sequentially**. Read-only and error UCs (1, 4, 10) can run in parallel. Test quests are named `e2e-r{round}-uc{n}`.
- Each run appends issues to `$SCRATCH/e2e/issues.md` (id, severity, UC, skill section, evidence, repro).
- **One gate for you:** before the first activation or event that pays out on testnet, I confirm with you once.

## Phase 3: fixes (a separate subagent per round)
- Input: open issues from `issues.md`. It edits `skills/quest-setup/**` + the `.cursor/skills` mirror, and runs `.github/scripts/validate_skills.py`.
- I read the short diff summary and commit on `QP-2890-verification`, one commit per round, `git add` only the skill paths (the existing uncommitted `validate_skills.py`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/*` stay untouched). No push.
- Issues that need server-side changes (onboarding for 316111, API bugs) go into the "external" section and are not fixed in the skill.

## Phase 4: retests
Fresh subagents: first the affected UCs, then a full regression of all UCs. Loop until clean: 0 open issues of any severity. Guard: if the same issue survives 2 fixes, I stop and come to you.

## Phase 5: report
`$SCRATCH/e2e/report.md`: UCs × rounds (pass/fail), all issues and their status, the external blockers, and a "fix → which stack PR it belongs to" map (#39 skeleton/auth, #40 document, #41 conditions, #42 rewards, #43 events, verification). Push/re-slicing across the stack only with your ok. At the end I deactivate the test quests (UC12).

## Verification
Done = the last full regression passes every UC with no new issues, and the web3_token/web3_item UCs reach a COMPLETED action with a tx hash in qp-data. The validator is green, and the commits contain only skill files.

content.text:
Сабагент проверил код и stage. По каждому ключу ниже: какой запрос, что ответил сервер, почему так и какой коммит это внёс.

## Что задеплоено на stage
На stage `/openapi.json` отдаёт маршруты `/projects/{project_id}/onboard`, `/merchants/{merchant_id}/projects` и `/publisher-credentials/validate`. Они есть только в ветке `origin/gas-token-launch`, где появились с MR !5568 (`QP-2864-publisher-human-lane`, Farid смёржил 2026-09-23). В `dev` их нет. Точный задеплоенный SHA сабагент не нашёл: `/version` отдаёт 404, а stage deploy pipeline он не смотрел. Вывод, что на stage именно эта ветка, сделан по набору маршрутов.

## Ключ 1: service key `93cf2bf8…` (X-REQUEST-APIKEY) → 401 "Invalid API key". Баг

**Запрос:**
```
GET /api/v2/accounts/f1a5f475-…/quests?limit=1
X-REQUEST-APIKEY: [REDACTED:credential]…
→ 401 {"error":"Invalid API key"}
```

**Причина:**
- Проверка стоит в `qp-server/internal/http/middleware/middleware.go:351-357`. Её внёс коммит `6307bd8653` (QP-2846, Farid, 2026-09-21, вошёл в !5568). Если у активного ключа `service_identity_id IS NULL`, middleware отдаёт 401 и пишет в лог `validate_api_key.no_service_identity`.
- Миграция `000014_service_identities.up.sql` один раз заполнила identity для ключей, которые существовали на момент миграции.
- Код, который создаёт ключи, не обновили. Ни один из этих путей не создаёт service identity и не привязывает её к ключу:
  - `repository/postgres/account.go:109` `CreateInWorkspace`. Твой аккаунт создан этим путём (`POST /workspaces/{id}/accounts`): у него role service и есть workspace_id.
  - `account.go:35` `CreateWithMasterKey`
  - `service/apikey.go:43` `Create`
- Поэтому любой ключ, созданный после миграции 000014, сразу не работает. Твой создан сегодня в 11:26 UTC, у него `service_identity_id = null`.

**Вторая проблема за первой (сабагент видел её в коде, но не проверял запросом):** `CreateInWorkspace` по-прежнему записывает role grant с `GranteeID = account.ID` (`account.go:146`, и так же на `:79`). А `granteeOf` (`auth/authorize.go:61`, QP-2847) теперь ищет гранты по id service identity. Значит, даже если привязать identity, ключ пройдёт аутентификацию, но не получит capabilities и будет ловить 403.

**Где ещё есть баг:** в `gas-token-launch`, `QP-2871-client-sdk-basic-credential` и `tech/get-publisher-details-to-quest`.

**Как чинить:**
- Каждый путь создания ключа должен вставлять строку в `service_identities` (`owner_kind=account`, `credential_source=qp_m2m`) и записывать её id в `api_keys.service_identity_id`.
- Role grant нужно писать на id identity, а не аккаунта.
- Для ключей, которые уже созданы без identity (включая твой), нужен повторный backfill.

## Ключ 2: project key 316111 (Basic) → 404 "Project not found". Не баг, проект не подключён

**Запрос:**
```
GET /api/v2/projects/316111/quests?limit=2
Authorization: Basic base64("939308:ac6f…")
→ 404 {"error":"Project not found"}
```

**Почему:**
- `service/project_scope.go:192-225` `resolveProjectScope` сначала ищет аккаунт с `accounts.xsolla_project_id = 316111`. Это происходит до проверки ключа в Xsolla (`:117`).
- Такого аккаунта нет: у твоего Rauf sandbox `xsolla_project_id = null`. Поэтому сервер отвечает 404 ещё до проверки ключа, и неверный ключ даёт тот же 404.
- Одинаковый 404 для неизвестных и неподключённых проектов сделан намеренно, чтобы по ответу нельзя было перебрать id проектов. Логика пришла из коммитов `8b62b6e152` (QP-2860) и `a0cf56bc6c` (QP-2862).

**Чтобы проект 316111 заработал, в базе должны быть:**
- workspace с `xsolla_merchant_id = 939308`
- активный аккаунт с `xsolla_project_id = 316111` в этом workspace
- строка в `service_identities` с `credential_source = '[REDACTED:credential]'` на этом аккаунте или workspace

**Как подключить:** `POST /api/v2/projects/316111/onboard` с твоим Basic и телом `{"merchant_name": …, "project_name": …}` (QP-2868, коммит `e95e446a15`). Это запись, поэтому сабагент её не отправлял. После подключения неверный ключ должен давать 401, а не 404.

## Черновик сообщения Фариду
> Farid, привет! На stage (gas-token-launch, после !5568) любой X-REQUEST-APIKEY, созданный после миграции 000014, получает 401 "Invalid API key". `CreateInWorkspace`, `CreateWithMasterKey` и `apiKeyService.Create` не создают и не привязывают service identity. К тому же они до сих пор пишут role grant на id аккаунта, а `granteeOf` теперь ищет по id identity. Можешь поправить create-пути, чтобы они создавали identity и писали grant на неё, и прогнать backfill для уже созданных ключей? Мой, например, 93cf2bf8-….

## Что это значит для плана
- Скилл как раз рассчитан на Basic, так что это основной lane для тестов. Его можно включить без Фарида, одним вызовом `/onboard`.
- Service key не работает, пока Фарид не починит баг.
- В скилле нет сценария подключения проекта и нет маршрутов `/projects/{id}/quests`, `/onboard` и `/publisher-credentials/validate`. Это уже первые находки для фиксов.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

content.text:
Это не проверенный факт, а догадка сабагента. Я передал её тебе как факт, это моя ошибка.

- **Откуда она взялась.** Сабагент посмотрел на строку аккаунта, которую ты прислал (`role: service`, заполнен `workspace_id`), и нашёл в коде путь создания, который даёт такую форму: `CreateInWorkspace`. Как именно создавался этот аккаунт, он не проверял: ни логов, ни истории запросов не смотрел. Проверено только одно: у ключа `service_identity_id = null`, и middleware на этом отдаёт 401. Этот вывод держится, каким бы путём ни создали ключ.
- **Про какой это ключ.** Речь только про service key `93cf2bf8…` и аккаунт "Rauf sandbox". Это строки из собственной базы QP (`accounts` и `api_keys`), ты сам прислал их вторым набором кредов. Ответ по коду qp-server. Где что-то выведено, а не проверено, я это помечаю.

**Ключ, созданный на сайте Publisher Account, в QP не создаётся.** Это обычный project API key Xsolla, и хранится он в Xsolla. QP его у себя не держит: у QP нет таблицы для таких ключей, он только проверяет их удалённо:
- `qp-server/internal/auth/xsolla_key_verifier.go:140-160` пробрасывает твой `Basic merchant_id:api_key` в GET на `XSOLLA_KEY_VALIDATION_URL`;
- на stage этот URL задан в `environments/stage/configs/configs.yaml:45` как `https://api.xsolla.com/merchant/current/projects/{project_id}/api_key/validate`;
- ответ 200 значит «ключ валиден», а 401, 403 или 404 значат «невалиден».

**Сам QP хранит только привязку тенантов**, то есть какой мерчант и проект Xsolla относятся к какому workspace и аккаунту QP: `workspaces.xsolla_merchant_id`, `accounts.xsolla_project_id` и `service_identities` с `credential_source = '[REDACTED:credential]'`.

**Publisher Account в QP не ходит.** В adtech сабагент не нашёл ни вебхука при создании ключа, ни автоподключения проекта при первом запросе. Код самого PA он не смотрел, так что это проверено только со стороны QP.

**Почему 404 для 316111.** В QP нет аккаунта, привязанного к этому проекту. `service/project_scope.go:195-199` отдаёт 404 до обращения в Xsolla и сам ничего не создаёт. Создать привязку можно только разовым вызовом `POST /api/v2/projects/316111/onboard`. По описанию эндпоинта его один раз вызывает сам паблишер, с Basic-ключом или через вход в PA.

**Возможный второй подвох (вывод, не проверено).** Stage QP проверяет ключи через **продовый** `api.xsolla.com`. Если ключ, выпущенный на publisher-client-**stage**, прод не знает, то даже после onboard запросы получат 401. Тогда это вопрос к Фариду про конфиг stage.

**Service key `93cf2bf8`** лежит во внутренней таблице QP `api_keys` (`db/migrations/000002_create_api_keys.up.sql:1`) и с PA никак не связан. Баг с ним (ключ создан без service identity, отсюда 401) по-прежнему на стороне Фарида.

Второй подвох можно проверить одним GET на этот validate URL с твоим Basic. Он ничего не меняет, но отправляет ключ на прод `api.xsolla.com`, поэтому без твоего ок не делаю. Проверить?

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

**Xsolla Quest Platform (QP)** — a Go microservices monorepo. The "QP" prefix denotes services owned by the QP team; other services without this prefix are maintained by separate teams.

## Common Commands

### Root-Level (Docker Compose)
```bash
make qp-up       # Start Quest Platform core services + run DB migrations
make up          # Start ALL services (including non-QP services)
make dev         # Start all services and wait for readiness
make health      # Check health of all running services
make qp-migrate  # Run DB migrations for Quest Platform only
```

### Per-Service (run from service directory)
```bash
make build            # Build static Linux binary (musl/amd64)
make run              # Run locally with default profile
make run-local        # Run with local config profile
make test-unit        # Unit tests only (fast)
make test-functional  # Functional/behavioral tests
make test-integration # Integration tests (requires containers)
make validate         # build + all tests + lint + merge coverage
make lint             # golangci-lint v2.5.0
make clean            # Remove build artifacts
```

### Postman Collections
Run before committing if you changed any HTTP endpoints:
```bash
make qp-generate-postman        # regenerate all 3 QP service collections (run from repo root)
make generate-postman           # regenerate this service only (run from service directory)
```
Collections output to `{service}/postman/collection.json`.
Scenario request bodies are defined in `{service}/postman/scenarios.json`.

### Run a Single Test
```bash
# From service directory:
go test ./internal/... -run TestFunctionName -v
```

### Devtools

Local helpers for inspecting staging infrastructure — sources under `devtools/`.

**Kafka UI for qp-stage** (`devtools/qp/kafka/stage/`):
```bash
make kafka-ui-up    # Start Kafka UI at http://localhost:8080
make kafka-ui-down  # Stop the container
make kafka-ui-logs  # Tail container logs
```
First-time setup: create `devtools/qp/kafka/stage/.env.secrets` with `KAFKA_USERNAME` and `KAFKA_PASSWORD` (file is gitignored). The image (`Dockerfile.kafka-ui`) bakes the Xsolla private CA into a PKCS12 truststore at build time, and `docker-compose.yaml` connects to `gnl-mq-kafka-qp-stage-0{1,2,3}.local:9092` over SASL_SSL/PLAIN.

### Shared Library Changes
When modifying anything in `lib/`, use the `publish-lib` skill to tag new versions and update dependent services' `go.mod` files. The libs are published to the internal GitLab package registry and imported by services as versioned modules (e.g., `gitlab.loc/adtech/adtech/lib/qp_health_check v0.3.5`).

## Load Testing Safety

> **STOP — read this before sending any events to the pipeline.**

**Do not run unsanctioned load tests against dev, stage, or production.** Use the rigs in `qp-load-testing/` for any sanctioned load test; they already follow the conventions below.

### Per-event bypass (required for smoke tests, debugging, reproductions)

Any event payload you send for testing purposes **must** include:

```json
"properties": { "load_test": "true" }
```

When both `LOAD_TEST_BYPASS_ENABLED=true` (already set in dev/stage; `false` in prod) and `properties.load_test == "true"`, quest-engine skips `StartGenericQuestWorkflow` entirely — no Temporal workflow is started, no Temporal Cloud cost is incurred. **Without this flag, every event starts a real, billable workflow.**

See [quest-engine/CLAUDE.md](quest-engine/CLAUDE.md) for the full bypass mechanism, exact file locations, and env var details.

### Full Temporal disable (nuclear option — local only)

Setting `TEMPORAL_DISABLED=true` in quest-engine swaps the Temporal client for a `NoOpWorkflowService`. Every workflow start across all flows (GenericQuest, OFW conversion, MMP, CS) becomes a no-op debug log. Use only for local reproductions — never on a shared environment.

See [quest-engine/CLAUDE.md](quest-engine/CLAUDE.md) for wiring details.

### Per-service notes

- [quest-engine/CLAUDE.md](quest-engine/CLAUDE.md) — owns both safeguards; full operational detail
- [qp-events-collector/CLAUDE.md](qp-events-collector/CLAUDE.md) — ingestion-side reminder
- [qp-worker-generic-quest/CLAUDE.md](qp-worker-generic-quest/CLAUDE.md) — worker-side reminder

## Architecture

### Service Structure

**QP team** (QP-prefixed):
```
qp-server/                   # REST API gateway (health, lifecycle)
qp-events-collector/         # Ingest events from external sources
qp-consumer-service/         # Kafka consumer → forwards to quest-engine
quest-engine/                # Core quest logic, rewards, Temporal workflows
qp-worker-generic-quest/     # Temporal worker for GENERIC_QUEST_TASK_QUEUE (QP-237 Phase 1)
qp-worker-conversion/        # Temporal worker for conversion workflows
```

**Offerwall team**
```
adtech-server/               # Core offerwall API server
events-collector/            # MMP event ingestion
events-relay/                # MMP event relay service to Braze/Amplitude
consumer-service/            # MMP event consumer and processor
```

**Shared libraries**
```
lib/                         # Shared Go modules (published to GitLab registry)
```

**Other active services** (co-located, separate team ownership — all are active and in scope for repo-wide work):
```
choices-service/             # Choices/offers service
social-quests/               # Social quests API
notification-service/        # Notification delivery
gift-cards-shop/             # Gift cards service
xsolla-app-backend/          # Xsolla app backend
xsolla-app-windows-backend/  # Xsolla app windows backend (XPWB)
```

#### XPW Project acronyms (XPWA / XPWB)
| Acronym | Project | Path |
|---|---|---|
| **XPWA** | Xsolla App Windows (frontend/desktop app) | [frontend/apps/xsolla-app-windows/](frontend/apps/xsolla-app-windows/) |
| **XPWB** | Xsolla App Windows Backend | [xsolla-app-windows-backend/](xsolla-app-windows-backend/) |

### Service Bootstrap Order (all services follow this pattern)
1. Load config from `environments/{profile}/configs/configs.yaml`
2. Initialize logger (`lib/qp_logger`)
3. Initialize OpenTelemetry tracing/metrics (Datadog exporter)
4. Setup health checker daemon (`lib/qp_health_check`)
5. Connect infrastructure (PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, ClickHouse, Temporal); quest-engine uses `bootstrap.InitInfra()` returning an `InfraDeps` struct
6. Wire repositories → services → workers/HTTP handlers
7. Start Fiber HTTP server on port `8080` (internal)
8. Register graceful shutdown handlers

### Configuration
- YAML files in `environments/{profile}/configs/configs.yaml`
- Profiles: `default` (production), `dev`, `stage`, `local`
- Switch profile with CLI flag: `-profile local`
- Supports environment variable substitution in YAML

### Observability Stack
- **Tracing/Metrics**: OpenTelemetry → Datadog exporter
- **Logging**: Logrus via `lib/qp_logger`
- **Health**: `/api/health` endpoint on every service; daemon polls component health and emits `healthcheck.status` and `healthcheck.component.reachable` OTel gauges. Wire via `HealthCheckConfig{Meter: telemetry.Meter}`.
- **Analytics**: ClickHouse (also used for event storage/querying in qp-consumer-service and quest-engine)
- **Dashboard**: `scripts/quest_platform_dashboard.json` — importable Datadog dashboard "Quest Platform - Engineering Operations" covering all 4 QP services; cluster `gcp-k8s-xsolla-prod`; includes widgets for `healthcheck.status`, `healthcheck.component.reachable`, all custom service metrics, Go runtime (scheduler latency P99, DB pool utilization, connection wait duration P95), and infrastructure (PG, Redis, ClickHouse, RabbitMQ)

| `adtech-server` | `adtech_server.partner_pause.offer_blocked.count` | Counter | Individual offers refused outright by an active partner pause (OFWTECH-2460); attributes: `partner`, `level`, `path` (only `campaign_details`/`participate` — the listing paths filter in SQL and have no single-offer rejection to count), `placement_id`. This is the exact served-offer-volume effect the ticket's observability AC asks for, scoped to the two paths where it can be counted precisely |
| `adtech-server` | `adtech_server.partner_pause.tester_bypass.count` | Counter | Requests where a **designated tester** was let through an active partner pause instead of being filtered/rejected (OFWTECH-2465); same attributes as `enforced.count` (`partner`, `level`, `path`, `placement_id`, `publisher_id`). A tester is an Xsolla account whose JWKS-verified token `username` is in `PARTNER_PAUSE_TESTER_XSOLLA_USERNAMES` (config, comma-separated; empty ⇒ feature off). Fires per resolved-set partner on listing/my_games/saved, and per bypassed campaign's partner on campaign_details/participate; the tester and non-tester counters are mutually exclusive on a given request, so a non-zero count here is tester traffic only — never ordinary users, who stay on `enforced`/`offer_blocked`. On the listing path a tester's request is additionally forced off the shared listing cache onto the direct decomposed path (the cache key omits `PausedPartners`), so tester traffic neither reads nor writes the entry ordinary users share |
| `adtech-server` | `adtech_server.banned_user.action.count` | Counter | Ops re-enable (unban) actions on the IAF banned-users surface (OFWTECH-2434); attributes: `action` (`unban`), `ban_source`, `outcome` (`success`/`failed`), `placement_id`/`publisher_id` (omitted when empty). `gamer_id` is deliberately **not** an attribute — unbounded cardinality. A rising count at `ban_source=earn_cap` or `conversion_velocity` is the signal that a fraud threshold is producing false positives and needs retuning via fraud-settings (OFWTECH-2435), not that Ops is misusing the tool |
| `adtech-server` | `adtech_server.banned_user.redis_clear.count` | Counter | quest-engine velocity-key clears attempted during an unban; attribute: `outcome` (`ok`/`failed`). Every `earn_cap`/`conversion_velocity` unban must clear `quest-engine:velocity:blocked:*`, which is written with **no TTL** — an unban whose clear fails would look successful to Ops but be reverted on the user's next conversion, so the service aborts the unban and this counter is how that shows up. `verisoul`/`publisher` bans leave no velocity state and are not counted here |

All `NewClickHouseDB(meter)`, `NewEventMapper(meter)`, `NewHealthChecker(config)`, `NewLedgerActivity(db, meter)`, `NewActionActivity(..., meter)`, `NewInflightMetricActivity(meter)`, and activity constructors accept a `metric.Meter`; pass `nil` to get a no-op meter (safe for tests).

#### PostgreSQL OTel Pool Metrics
When `TelemetryEnabled=true`, both `qp-server` and `quest-engine` use `otelsql.Register()` (via `github.com/XSAM/otelsql`) to wrap the SQL driver, which instruments individual SQL call spans. `otelsql.RegisterDBStatsMetrics` IS called in both services (`quest-engine/internal/repository/postgre/database.go:151`, `qp-server/internal/repository/postgres/postgres.go:153`), emitting standard `db.client.connections.*` pool stats metrics.

Driver differences:
- `qp-server`: uses `gorm.io/driver/postgres` for both plain and telemetry paths — that driver's own default (no `DriverName` override) opens via pgx (`jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib`), not `lib/pq`; a constraint violation surfaces as `*pgconn.PgError` (confirmed by the CHECK-violation translation in `internal/repository/postgres/role_grant.go`, QP-2644)
- `quest-engine`: uses `pgx` (`jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib`) when `TelemetryEnabled=true`, falls back to `gorm.io/driver/postgres` otherwise (same pgx-underneath default applies there too when it does)

Connection setup differences:
- `qp-server`: 5 retries (exponential backoff); runs `db.RunMigrations` inline after connect (warns on failure, does not abort); pool configured from `config.Props` (DBMaxOpenConns/DBMaxIdleConns/DBConnMaxLifetime), defaults to 25 open / 5 idle / 5 min when zero; sslMode from `config.Props.DBSSLModeEnabled` ("disable" or "require")
- `quest-engine`: retries from `config.Props.DBMaxRetries`; validates host/user/db/port non-empty before connecting; DSN includes `search_path` via `DBSchema` config field; sslMode hardcoded to "prefer"; pool set via `configureConnectionPool()` helper (applies config values directly — no zero-value fallback defaults)

OTel attribute differences:
- `qp-server`: `NetworkPeerAddressKey` = `DBHost`
- `quest-engine`: `NetworkPeerAddressKey` = `"DBHost:DBPort"` (URL format)

The `quest-engine` `PostgresDB` additionally exposes `GetSQLDB() (*sql.DB, error)` and `IsConnected() bool` for external health/metrics use.

### Infrastructure Dependencies
PostgreSQL · Redis · Kafka (+ Zookeeper for QP) · Temporal · ClickHouse · RabbitMQ (legacy)

- ClickHouse is **optional** in quest-engine: initialization is skipped when `ClickHouseHost` is not configured.
- Health check components registered per service: Redis, ClickHouse, Kafka producer/consumer, RabbitMQ (quest-engine), Postgres (quest-engine, qp-server).

### HTTP Layer
- Framework: **Fiber v2**
- API docs: **Huma v2** (OpenAPI/Swagger)
- Internal port: `8080` (all services)
- OpenAPI/docs routes (`/docs`, `/openapi-3.0.json`, etc.) are blocked with 404 in production (`ENV=prod`) for qp-events-collector
- Idempotency middleware (`gofiber/contrib/idempotency`) enabled on qp-events-collector
- qp-events-collector `router.New(kafkaProducer, healthChecker, meter)` accepts a `metric.Meter` for per-handler OTel instrumentation

#### Fiber zero-copy headers — `strings.Clone` before retaining (OFWTECH-1535)
Fiber runs with `Immutable: false`, so `ctx.Header()`/`c.Get()`/`c.Query()`/`c.Params()` return strings aliasing the fasthttp request buffer, which is reused by the next request. **Always `strings.Clone(...)` such a value before it outlives the handler** — stored in the request context, emitted on an async/fire-and-forget event, or used as a key/input to a long-lived or global cache (e.g. the global `uap-go` UA parser). Skipping the clone silently leaks one request's data into another's. Examples: `UserAgentMiddleware`, `ExtractTrackingDataMiddleware`, `FunnelEventMiddleware` in `adtech-server/config/middleware.go`.

### Authentication & Authorization (qp-server)
qp-server enforces a scoped capability model on its management API: a dual-lane `Authenticate` middleware (human SSO Bearer JWT vs. service `X-REQUEST-APIKEY`) resolves callers to a lane-agnostic `Principal`, and `RequireCaps` checks that Principal's role-derived capabilities against an `account`/`workspace` scope before allowing account, grant, API-key, and quest-config mutations. Some routes (cross-service bulk quest reads, key self-validation, all of `subscriptions/*`) intentionally or provisionally still use the legacy master-role/API-key-only middleware. See [qp-server/CLAUDE.md](qp-server/CLAUDE.md#authentication--authorization) for the full model and per-route migration status. Other services authenticate to qp-server as the service lane via `lib/client-sdk`.

### Deployment Tags (GitLab CI)
Tag format determines what gets deployed where:
```
dev-qp-v1.2.3                                  → Dev, quest-engine + adtech-server, consumer-service, events-collector, events-relay, qp-worker-generic-quest (NOT qp-server/qp-ec/qp-cs, NOT qp-worker-conversion)
dev-all-v1.2.3                                 → Dev, all services
stage-qp-v1.2.3                                → Stage, quest-engine + adtech-server, consumer-service, events-collector, events-relay, qp-worker-conversion, qp-worker-generic-quest (NOT qp-server/qp-ec/qp-cs)
stage-adtech-qp-all-v*                         → Stage, ALL 5 QP HTTP services (qp-server, qp-ec, qp-cs, quest-engine, qp-data)
stage-adtech-qp-server-v*                      → Stage, qp-server only
stage-adtech-qp-ec-v*                          → Stage, qp-events-collector only
stage-adtech-qp-cs-v*                          → Stage, qp-consumer-service only
stage-adtech-qp-data-v*                        → Stage, qp-data only
stage-qp-gqw-*                                 → Stage, qp-worker-generic-quest only
stage-adtech-offerwall-iaf-v*                  → Stage, offerwall-iaf only
v-qp-1.2.3                                     → Production, quest-engine + adtech-server, consumer-service, events-collector, events-relay, qp-worker-conversion, qp-worker-generic-quest (NOT qp-server/qp-ec/qp-cs)
v-adtech-qp-all-v*                             → Production, ALL 5 QP HTTP services (qp-server, qp-ec, qp-cs, quest-engine, qp-data)
v-adtech-qp-data-v*                            → Production, qp-data only
v-qp-gqw-*                                     → Production, qp-worker-generic-quest only
v-adtech-offerwall-iaf-v*                      → Production, offerwall-iaf only
v-quest-engine-1.2.3                           → Production, quest-engine only
```

> **Important**: `*-qp-*` tags (`dev-qp-*`, `stage-qp-*`, `v-qp-*`) are matched by regex in each service's own `gitlab-ci.yml` (e.g. `/^(stage-all|stage-qp|stage-<service>).*$/`), so a single `-qp-` tag fans out to every service whose CI opts into that pattern — currently: `quest-engine`, `adtech-server`, `consumer-service`, `events-collector`, `events-relay`, `qp-worker-generic-quest` (dev/stage/prod), plus `qp-worker-conversion` (stage/prod only). It does **not** cover `qp-server`, `qp-events-collector` (the QP-prefixed one), `qp-consumer-service`, or `qp-data` — those need `stage-adtech-qp-all-*` or their own `stage-adtech-qp-{server,ec,cs,data}-*` tag. `qp-data` deploys to **stage and prod only** (it has no `dev` environment), so no `dev-*` tag deploys it. Verify against each service's `gitlab-ci.yml` `deploy_stage`/`deploy_prod` rules before assuming scope — this list can drift as services adopt/drop the shared pattern.

CI config: root `.gitlab-ci.yml` is an orchestrator that triggers service-specific `<service>/gitlab-ci.yml` files.

### Post-Release Automation (QP-2219)
After production deployment (`v-*` tags) of any QP service, a `post_release` stage runs automatically:
1. **Release notes** generated from commits since previous release → `release-notes.md` artifact
2. **Slack notification** posted to `#qp-releases` with Block Kit formatted message
3. **Claude-driven adtech docs MR** — analyzes the tag-to-tag diff via the Anthropic API and opens an MR in `adtech/adtech` proposing updates to `CLAUDE.md`, `${SERVICE}/CLAUDE.md`, and `scripts/SCRIPTS_DOCUMENTATION.md` wherever the diff makes them inaccurate.
4. **Claude-driven claude-config skill PR** — analyzes the same diff and opens a PR in `github.com/xsolla/claude-config` updating `skills/public/xsolla/quest-platform/SKILL.md` when public behavior, APIs, or contracts have changed.

Both Claude-driven jobs use structured tool output for deterministic patching, idempotent branch names, and `allow_failure: true` so a Claude hiccup never blocks a release.

CI config: `ci/templates/post-release.yml` (shared template included by all 4 QP service CIs)
Scripts: `scripts/shell/generate-release-notes.sh`, `notify-slack-release.sh`, `claude-propose-adtech-docs.sh`, `claude-propose-claude-config-skill.sh`

Required CI variables:
- `QP_RELEASES_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` — Slack Incoming Webhook (masked)
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — Anthropic API key (masked)
- `GITLAB_API_TOKEN` — GitLab PAT/PrAT with `api` scope (masked) — for opening MRs
- `GITHUB_TOKEN_CLAUDE_CONFIG` — GitHub fine-grained PAT with Contents+PR write on `xsolla/claude-config` (masked) — for opening PRs

### Testing Structure
Each service follows:
```
internal/          # Unit-testable business logic
test/functional/   # Behavior tests
test/integration/  # Container-based integration tests
e2e/               # End-to-end (quest-engine has e2e/generic_quest/)
```
Coverage profiles are merged via `gocovmerge` for SonarQube.

**quest-engine exception**: `test/integration/` uses Temporal's in-process `testsuite.TestWorkflowEnvironment` (no real containers). Activities are registered as inline stubs. Run with `make test-integration` from the `quest-engine/` directory.

## Code Standards (from `.cursor/rules/`)
- Cognitive complexity ≤ 15 per function
- Functions ≤ 7 parameters
- Descriptive names, early returns, minimal nesting
- Comments only for non-obvious rationale
- Fix root causes, not symptoms
- Run `make validate` before committing

### Logging & Trace Correlation
- Use `qp_logger.LoggerFromCtx(ctx)` whenever `context.Context` is available — never `qp_logger.Logger` directly in request handlers, Temporal activities, or any traced code path
- For fire-and-forget goroutines spawned from traced contexts, use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` to preserve trace ID without propagating cancellation
- `qp_logger.Logger` is acceptable only in startup/shutdown code, constructors, and background loops where no request trace exists

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Issues live in Jira at xsolla.atlassian.net, project `QP` (QP-XXXX tickets). See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Five canonical triage roles using default label strings. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Multi-context repo — each service has its own `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/`. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

**Xsolla Quest Platform (QP)** — a Go microservices monorepo. The "QP" prefix denotes services owned by the QP team; other services without this prefix are maintained by separate teams.

## Common Commands

### Root-Level (Docker Compose)
```bash
make qp-up       # Start Quest Platform core services + run DB migrations

```

### Per-Service (run from service directory)
```bash
make build            # Build static Linux binary (musl/amd64)
make run              # Run locally with default profile
make run-local        # Run with local config profile
make test-unit        # Unit tests only (fast)
make test-functional  # Functional/behavioral tests
make test-integration # Integration tests (requires containers)
make validate         # build + all tests + lint + merge coverage

```

Run before committing if you changed any HTTP endpoints:
```bash
make qp-generate-postman        # regenerate all 3 QP service collections (run from repo root)

```
Collections output to `{service}/postman/collection.json`.
Scenario request bodies are defined in `{service}/postman/scenarios.json`.

### Run a Single Test

```bash
go test ./internal/... -run TestFunctionName -v
```

### Devtools

Local helpers for inspecting staging infrastructure — sources under `devtools/`.

**Kafka UI for qp-stage** (`devtools/qp/kafka/stage/`):
```bash
make kafka-ui-up    # Start Kafka UI at http://localhost:8080
make kafka-ui-down  # Stop the container
make kafka-ui-logs  # Tail container logs
```
First-time setup: create `devtools/qp/kafka/stage/.env.secrets` with `KAFKA_USERNAME` and `KAFKA_PASSWORD` (file is gitignored). The image (`Dockerfile.kafka-ui`) bakes the Xsolla private CA into a PKCS12 truststore at build time, and `docker-compose.yaml` connects to `gnl-mq-kafka-qp-stage-0{1,2,3}.local:9092` over SASL_SSL/PLAIN.

### Shared Library Changes
When modifying anything in `lib/`, use the `publish-lib` skill to tag new versions and update dependent services' `go.mod` files. The libs are published to the internal GitLab package registry and imported by services as versioned modules (e.g., `gitlab.loc/adtech/adtech/lib/qp_health_check v0.3.5`).

## Load Testing Safety

> **STOP — read this before sending any events to the pipeline.**

**Do not run unsanctioned load tests against dev, stage, or production.** Use the rigs in `qp-load-testing/` for any sanctioned load test; they already follow the conventions below.

### Per-event bypass (required for smoke tests, debugging, reproductions)

Any event payload you send for testing purposes **must** include:

```json
"properties": { "load_test": "true" }
```

When both `LOAD_TEST_BYPASS_ENABLED=true` (already set in dev/stage; `false` in prod) and `properties.load_test == "true"`, quest-engine skips `StartGenericQuestWorkflow` entirely — no Temporal workflow is started, no Temporal Cloud cost is incurred. **Without this flag, every event starts a real, billable workflow.**

See [quest-engine/CLAUDE.md](quest-engine/CLAUDE.md) for the full bypass mechanism, exact file locations, and env var details.

### Full Temporal disable (nuclear option — local only)

Setting `TEMPORAL_DISABLED=true` in quest-engine swaps the Temporal client for a `NoOpWorkflowService`. Every workflow start across all flows (GenericQuest, OFW conversion, MMP, CS) becomes a no-op debug log. Use only for local reproductions — never on a shared environment.

See [quest-engine/CLAUDE.md](quest-engine/CLAUDE.md) for wiring details.

### Per-service notes

- [quest-engine/CLAUDE.md](quest-engine/CLAUDE.md) — owns both safeguards; full operational detail
- [qp-events-collector/CLAUDE.md](qp-events-collector/CLAUDE.md) — ingestion-side reminder
- [qp-worker-generic-quest/CLAUDE.md](qp-worker-generic-quest/CLAUDE.md) — worker-side reminder

## Architecture

### Service Structure

**QP team** (QP-prefixed):
```
qp-server/                   # REST API gateway (health, lifecycle)
qp-events-collector/         # Ingest events from external sources
qp-consumer-service/         # Kafka consumer → forwards to quest-engine
quest-engine/                # Core quest logic, rewards, Temporal workflows
qp-worker-generic-quest/     # Temporal worker for GENERIC_QUEST_TASK_QUEUE (QP-237 Phase 1)
qp-worker-conversion/        # Temporal worker for conversion workflows
```

**Offerwall team**
```
adtech-server/               # Core offerwall API server
events-collector/            # MMP event ingestion
events-relay/                # MMP event relay service to Braze/Amplitude
consumer-service/            # MMP event consumer and processor
```

**Shared libraries**
```
lib/                         # Shared Go modules (published to GitLab registry)
```

**Other active services** (co-located, separate team ownership — all are active and in scope for repo-wide work):
```
choices-service/             # Choices/offers service
social-quests/               # Social quests API
notification-service/        # Notification delivery
gift-cards-shop/             # Gift cards service
xsolla-app-backend/          # Xsolla app backend
xsolla-app-windows-backend/  # Xsolla app windows backend (XPWB)
```

#### XPW Project acronyms (XPWA / XPWB)
| Acronym | Project | Path |
|---|---|---|
| **XPWA** | Xsolla App Windows (frontend/desktop app) | [frontend/apps/xsolla-app-windows/](frontend/apps/xsolla-app-windows/) |
| **XPWB** | Xsolla App Windows Backend | [xsolla-app-windows-backend/](xsolla-app-windows-backend/) |

### Service Bootstrap Order (all services follow this pattern)
1. Load config from `environments/{profile}/configs/configs.yaml`
2. Initialize logger (`lib/qp_logger`)
3. Initialize OpenTelemetry tracing/metrics (Datadog exporter)
4. Setup health checker daemon (`lib/qp_health_check`)
5. Connect infrastructure (PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, ClickHouse, Temporal); quest-engine uses `bootstrap.InitInfra()` returning an `InfraDeps` struct
6. Wire repositories → services → workers/HTTP handlers
7. Start Fiber HTTP server on port `8080` (internal)
8. Register graceful shutdown handlers

### Configuration
- YAML files in `environments/{profile}/configs/configs.yaml`
- Profiles: `default` (production), `dev`, `stage`, `local`
- Switch profile with CLI flag: `-profile local`
- Supports environment variable substitution in YAML

### Key Shared Libraries
| Library | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `lib/qp_health_check` | Health check framework + OTel metrics + daemon |
| `lib/qp_logger` | Logrus wrapper with structured fields |
| `lib/qp_errors` | Centralized error types |
| `lib/kafka` | Kafka producer/consumer utilities |
| `lib/models/v2` | Shared protobuf-based data models |
| `lib/validation` | Input validation |
| `lib/caching` | Redis caching layer |
| `lib/client-sdk` | Clients for qp-server, currency API, gacha API, xsolla login |
| `lib/protobuf` | Protobuf definitions + generated Go code for events (v1/v2) and quest_conversion |
| `lib/utilities` | General-purpose helpers: math, strings, slices, date, UUID, Kafka config, pagination, etc. |

### Observability Stack
- **Tracing/Metrics**: OpenTelemetry → Datadog exporter

- **Health**: `/api/health` endpoint on every service; daemon polls component health and emits `healthcheck.status` and `healthcheck.component.reachable` OTel gauges. Wire via `HealthCheckConfig{Meter: telemetry.Meter}`.
- **Analytics**: ClickHouse (also used for event storage/querying in qp-consumer-service and quest-engine)
- **Dashboard**: `scripts/quest_platform_dashboard.json` — importable Datadog dashboard "Quest Platform - Engineering Operations" covering all 4 QP services; cluster `gcp-k8s-xsolla-prod`; includes widgets for `healthcheck.status`, `healthcheck.component.reachable`, all custom service metrics, Go runtime (scheduler latency P99, DB pool utilization, connection wait duration P95), and infrastructure (PG, Redis, ClickHouse, RabbitMQ)

#### PostgreSQL OTel Pool Metrics
When `TelemetryEnabled=true`, both `qp-server` and `quest-engine` use `otelsql.Register()` (via `github.com/XSAM/otelsql`) to wrap the SQL driver, which instruments individual SQL call spans. `otelsql.RegisterDBStatsMetrics` IS called in both services (`quest-engine/internal/repository/postgre/database.go:151`, `qp-server/internal/repository/postgres/postgres.go:153`), emitting standard `db.client.connections.*` pool stats metrics.

Driver differences:
- `qp-server`: uses `gorm.io/driver/postgres` for both plain and telemetry paths — that driver's own default (no `DriverName` override) opens via pgx (`jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib`), not `lib/pq`; a constraint violation surfaces as `*pgconn.PgError` (confirmed by the CHECK-violation translation in `internal/repository/postgres/role_grant.go`, QP-2644)
- `quest-engine`: uses `pgx` (`jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib`) when `TelemetryEnabled=true`, falls back to `gorm.io/driver/postgres` otherwise (same pgx-underneath default applies there too when it does)

Connection setup differences:
- `qp-server`: 5 retries (exponential backoff); runs `db.RunMigrations` inline after connect (warns on failure, does not abort); pool configured from `config.Props` (DBMaxOpenConns/DBMaxIdleConns/DBConnMaxLifetime), defaults to 25 open / 5 idle / 5 min when zero; sslMode from `config.Props.DBSSLModeEnabled` ("disable" or "require")
- `quest-engine`: retries from `config.Props.DBMaxRetries`; validates host/user/db/port non-empty before connecting; DSN includes `search_path` via `DBSchema` config field; sslMode hardcoded to "prefer"; pool set via `configureConnectionPool()` helper (applies config values directly — no zero-value fallback defaults)

OTel attribute differences:
- `qp-server`: `NetworkPeerAddressKey` = `DBHost`
- `quest-engine`: `NetworkPeerAddressKey` = `"DBHost:DBPort"` (URL format)

The `quest-engine` `PostgresDB` additionally exposes `GetSQLDB() (*sql.DB, error)` and `IsConnected() bool` for external health/metrics use.

### Infrastructure Dependencies
PostgreSQL · Redis · Kafka (+ Zookeeper for QP) · Temporal · ClickHouse · RabbitMQ (legacy)

- ClickHouse is **optional** in quest-engine: initialization is skipped when `ClickHouseHost` is not configured.
- Health check components registered per service: Redis, ClickHouse, Kafka producer/consumer, RabbitMQ (quest-engine), Postgres (quest-engine, qp-server).

### HTTP Layer
- Framework: **Fiber v2**
- API docs: **Huma v2** (OpenAPI/Swagger)
- Internal port: `8080` (all services)
- OpenAPI/docs routes (`/docs`, `/openapi-3.0.json`, etc.) are blocked with 404 in production (`ENV=prod`) for qp-events-collector
- Idempotency middleware (`gofiber/contrib/idempotency`) enabled on qp-events-collector
- qp-events-collector `router.New(kafkaProducer, healthChecker, meter)` accepts a `metric.Meter` for per-handler OTel instrumentation

#### Fiber zero-copy headers — `strings.Clone` before retaining (OFWTECH-1535)
Fiber runs with `Immutable: false`, so `ctx.Header()`/`c.Get()`/`c.Query()`/`c.Params()` return strings aliasing the fasthttp request buffer, which is reused by the next request. **Always `strings.Clone(...)` such a value before it outlives the handler** — stored in the request context, emitted on an async/fire-and-forget event, or used as a key/input to a long-lived or global cache (e.g. the global `uap-go` UA parser). Skipping the clone silently leaks one request's data into another's. Examples: `UserAgentMiddleware`, `ExtractTrackingDataMiddleware`, `FunnelEventMiddleware` in `adtech-server/config/middleware.go`.

### Authentication & Authorization (qp-server)
qp-server enforces a scoped capability model on its management API: a dual-lane `Authenticate` middleware (human SSO Bearer JWT vs. service `X-REQUEST-APIKEY`) resolves callers to a lane-agnostic `Principal`, and `RequireCaps` checks that Principal's role-derived capabilities against an `account`/`workspace` scope before allowing account, grant, API-key, and quest-config mutations. Some routes (cross-service bulk quest reads, key self-validation, all of `subscriptions/*`) intentionally or provisionally still use the legacy master-role/API-key-only middleware. See [qp-server/CLAUDE.md](qp-server/CLAUDE.md#authentication--authorization) for the full model and per-route migration status. Other services authenticate to qp-server as the service lane via `lib/client-sdk`.

### Deployment Tags (GitLab CI)
Tag format determines what gets deployed where:
```
dev-qp-v1.2.3                                  → Dev, quest-engine + adtech-server, consumer-service, events-collector, events-relay, qp-worker-generic-quest (NOT qp-server/qp-ec/qp-cs, NOT qp-worker-conversion)
dev-all-v1.2.3                                 → Dev, all services
stage-qp-v1.2.3                                → Stage, quest-engine + adtech-server, consumer-service, events-collector, events-relay, qp-worker-conversion, qp-worker-generic-quest (NOT qp-server/qp-ec/qp-cs)
stage-adtech-qp-all-v*                         → Stage, ALL 5 QP HTTP services (qp-server, qp-ec, qp-cs, quest-engine, qp-data)
stage-adtech-qp-server-v*                      → Stage, qp-server only
stage-adtech-qp-ec-v*                          → Stage, qp-events-collector only
stage-adtech-qp-cs-v*                          → Stage, qp-consumer-service only
stage-adtech-qp-data-v*                        → Stage, qp-data only
stage-qp-gqw-*                                 → Stage, qp-worker-generic-quest only
stage-adtech-offerwall-iaf-v*                  → Stage, offerwall-iaf only
v-qp-1.2.3                                     → Production, quest-engine + adtech-server, consumer-service, events-collector, events-relay, qp-worker-conversion, qp-worker-generic-quest (NOT qp-server/qp-ec/qp-cs)
v-adtech-qp-all-v*                             → Production, ALL 5 QP HTTP services (qp-server, qp-ec, qp-cs, quest-engine, qp-data)
v-adtech-qp-data-v*                            → Production, qp-data only
v-qp-gqw-*                                     → Production, qp-worker-generic-quest only
v-adtech-offerwall-iaf-v*                      → Production, offerwall-iaf only
v-quest-engine-1.2.3                           → Production, quest-engine only
```

> **Important**: `*-qp-*` tags (`dev-qp-*`, `stage-qp-*`, `v-qp-*`) are matched by regex in each service's own `gitlab-ci.yml` (e.g. `/^(stage-all|stage-qp|stage-<service>).*$/`), so a single `-qp-` tag fans out to every service whose CI opts into that pattern — currently: `quest-engine`, `adtech-server`, `consumer-service`, `events-collector`, `events-relay`, `qp-worker-generic-quest` (dev/stage/prod), plus `qp-worker-conversion` (stage/prod only). It does **not** cover `qp-server`, `qp-events-collector` (the QP-prefixed one), `qp-consumer-service`, or `qp-data` — those need `stage-adtech-qp-all-*` or their own `stage-adtech-qp-{server,ec,cs,data}-*` tag. `qp-data` deploys to **stage and prod only** (it has no `dev` environment), so no `dev-*` tag deploys it. Verify against each service's `gitlab-ci.yml` `deploy_stage`/`deploy_prod` rules before assuming scope — this list can drift as services adopt/drop the shared pattern.

CI config: root `.gitlab-ci.yml` is an orchestrator that triggers service-specific `<service>/gitlab-ci.yml` files.

### Post-Release Automation (QP-2219)
After production deployment (`v-*` tags) of any QP service, a `post_release` stage runs automatically:
1. **Release notes** generated from commits since previous release → `release-notes.md` artifact
2. **Slack notification** posted to `#qp-releases` with Block Kit formatted message
3. **Claude-driven adtech docs MR** — analyzes the tag-to-tag diff via the Anthropic API and opens an MR in `adtech/adtech` proposing updates to `CLAUDE.md`, `${SERVICE}/CLAUDE.md`, and `scripts/SCRIPTS_DOCUMENTATION.md` wherever the diff makes them inaccurate.
4. **Claude-driven claude-config skill PR** — analyzes the same diff and opens a PR in `github.com/xsolla/claude-config` updating `skills/public/xsolla/quest-platform/SKILL.md` when public behavior, APIs, or contracts have changed.

Both Claude-driven jobs use structured tool output for deterministic patching, idempotent branch names, and `allow_failure: true` so a Claude hiccup never blocks a release.

CI config: `ci/templates/post-release.yml` (shared template included by all 4 QP service CIs)
Scripts: `scripts/shell/generate-release-notes.sh`, `notify-slack-release.sh`, `claude-propose-adtech-docs.sh`, `claude-propose-claude-config-skill.sh`

Required CI variables:
- `QP_RELEASES_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` — Slack Incoming Webhook (masked)
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — Anthropic API key (masked)
- `GITLAB_API_TOKEN` — GitLab PAT/PrAT with `api` scope (masked) — for opening MRs
- `GITHUB_TOKEN_CLAUDE_CONFIG` — GitHub fine-grained PAT with Contents+PR write on `xsolla/claude-config` (masked) — for opening PRs

### Testing Structure
Each service follows:
```
internal/          # Unit-testable business logic
test/functional/   # Behavior tests
test/integration/  # Container-based integration tests
e2e/               # End-to-end (quest-engine has e2e/generic_quest/)
```
Coverage profiles are merged via `gocovmerge` for SonarQube.

**quest-engine exception**: `test/integration/` uses Temporal's in-process `testsuite.TestWorkflowEnvironment` (no real containers). Activities are registered as inline stubs. Run with `make test-integration` from the `quest-engine/` directory.

## Code Standards (from `.cursor/rules/`)
- Cognitive complexity ≤ 15 per function
- Functions ≤ 7 parameters
- Descriptive names, early returns, minimal nesting
- Comments only for non-obvious rationale
- Fix root causes, not symptoms
- Run `make validate` before committing

### Logging & Trace Correlation
- Use `qp_logger.LoggerFromCtx(ctx)` whenever `context.Context` is available — never `qp_logger.Logger` directly in request handlers, Temporal activities, or any traced code path
- For fire-and-forget goroutines spawned from traced contexts, use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` to preserve trace ID without propagating cancellation
- `qp_logger.Logger` is acceptable only in startup/shutdown code, constructors, and background loops where no request trace exists

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Issues live in Jira at xsolla.atlassian.net, project `QP` (QP-XXXX tickets). See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Five canonical triage roles using default label strings. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Multi-context repo — each service has its own `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/`. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

</system-reminder>
